questions: How many bars did you measure at 20 mK, on how many chips and cooldowns, and how many showed a polarity that reversed with [100] preparation? The paper shows two.
Why were the others set aside, if any were?
Which ranges did you measure beyond the ones shown: preparation fields above ±1 T along [100], temperatures above base, and small applied fields around zero after each preparation?
What does the second-best dataset look like, for example the [100] bar with histograms like Fig. 3a and 3b, or a second cooldown of the [010] bar?
What residual field, including its out-of-plane part, does your magnet leave at the sample after the ±1 T and ±4 T excursions along each axis, and was it measured or nulled?

Were both bars on the same chip in one mounting, with the [100] and [010] fields from different coils of a vector magnet? A chip tilt relative to each coil could give the same anisotropy in both bars; a 90° remount would separate crystal and magnet axes.

Do the preparation fields at which η changes sign in Fig. 3d match the switching fields of Reven in Fig. 4c, given that the reference bar comes from a CuMnAs wafer "with 3 nm fully oxidized Al cap" (p. 8) and was measured at 5 K?

How does η change with the 50 µV threshold and the 0.2 s step delay, which "was chosen empirically to minimize premature switching associated with faster current ramping" (p. 8), and what is the offset of the current-to-voltage converter?
